newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Adidas first quarter profits jump.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Adidas first quarter profits jump.

text.p: Adidas AG, the German sportswear maker, reaping the benefit of strong sales of training shoes and sports clothing, reported a 33 percent jump in first quarter net profit on Tuesday.

Investors, delighted with results, sent the group's shares up 3.5 percent in pre-bourse trading and helped the stock begin floor trading up 2.77 percent at 185.50 marks, outpacing the broader market's 1.53 percent gain.

The sportswear maker known for its three-striped logo said net profit rose to 169 million marks from 127 million marks ($73.5 million) in the first quarter of 1996. Simultaneously earnings for the group's common shares surged to 3.72 marks per share from 2.80 marks per share one year earlier.
Sales jumped 43.1 percent to 1.713 billion marks, the group said in a mandatory bourse statement.

On the other hand, Adidas also said marketing and administrative costs had jumped 47.5 percent to 481 million marks, largely driven by costs related to the promotion of a new brand of training shoes and the upcoming soccer world championship.
Earlier analysts had said Adidas' forecast that promotional expenses would continue to rise even as sales and profits would keep growing would be negative, although not overwhelming.

During the first quarter, traditionally one of the strongest quarters of the year for the group, Adidas posted a 32 percent jump in sport shoe sales to 785 million marks, with the brands "Running" and "Womens" leading the way.
The group's new shoe range called "Feet You Wear", introduced in the third quarter of 1996, continued to perform well, Adidas said.
Sportswear sales jumped 56 percent with womens and children's wear showing a particularly strong development.

Sales in the Asia/Pacific region, the group's fastest growing market, more than doubled to 183 million marks, Adidas said. Sales in North America jumped by 75 percent to 395 million marks and were largely buoyed by strong sales of the "Running" shoe brand and sportwear.
In Europe, still Adidas' largest market, the group's first quarter sales climbed by 29 percent to 1.1 billion marks.

Adidas, which traditionally makes no forecasts for the whole year, said that its inventory climbed by 20 percent to 971 million marks in the first quarter, growing at a slower pace than orders did. Orders rose by 36 percent during the first quarter Adidas said.
Industry analysts had said the group should post double-digit growth rates this year, especially after new running shoes are introduced, and after the year got off to a such a strong start.
